items.title: Asian Stocks to Slip With US CPI, Iran in Focus: Markets Wrap
items.author: Toby Alder
items.content: <article>Asian stocks were poised to follow Wall Street lower as traders held back from riskier bets ahead of key inflation data and remained wary over US-Iran developments.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 12
items.author: Kanoko Matsuyama and Charles Gorrivan
items.content: <article>Oil steadied after a four-day gain as traders monitored efforts for a deal that could help restore energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.</article>

items.title: Blackstone Strikes $1.8 Billion Deal for Air Canada Loyalty Unit
items.author: Thomas Seal and Stephanie Hughes
items.content: <article>Blackstone Inc. and a group of Canadian pension funds are buying a 25% stake in Air Canada’s Aeroplan loyalty program for C$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion).</article>

items.title: The Chinese AI Model Rattling Silicon Valley and Washington
items.content: <article>A new Chinese AI model is sending shockwaves through Silicon Valley and Washington. Today on Big Take Asia: What Moonshot’s controversial Kimi K3 means for the future of the global AI race.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Bitwise Cuts 14% of Jobs With Crypto Industry Under Pressure
items.author: Olga Kharif and Vildana Hajric
items.content: <article>Crypto firm Bitwise Asset Management Inc. has let go about 14% of its workforce during a prolonged slump in digital-asset prices.</article>

items.title: Pakistan Says Deal Is Close Even as Iran, US Harden Stances
items.content: <article>Pakistan’s defense minister said the US and Iran are “close to some sort of arrangement” over the Strait of Hormuz, even after both sides appeared to toughen their positions in the long-deadlocked negotiations. Noam Raydan, William Sudhaus Senior Fellow at The Near East Institute says the data  shows that the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea will remain essential choke points.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Fmr. FDA, CDC Official on Cyclospora, Food Safety Issues
items.content: <article>Steve Ostroff, Former Acting Commissioner of the FDA and Former Deputy Director of the National Center for Infectious Diseases at the CDC, joined the program to discuss the public awareness timeline of the cyclospora outbreak. The conversation highlighted that while the outbreak became widely known in early to mid-July, there were reports suggesting that government agencies had knowledge of the issue weeks prior to public disclosure. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Deep Dive Into The US' Critical Minerals Investment
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Senior Economic Statecraft Reporter Joe Deaux joins Tim Stenovec and Kristine Aquino for a one-hour special of Businessweek Daily to answer all your questions about rare earths and the $3 Billion US investment in the critical minerals industry. Investigative Reporter Polly Mosendz discusses her report on how "Trump Is Rewriting Corporate Norms With 211-Mile Arctic Road." Plus, Gracelin Baskaran -- Director of Critical Minerals Security Program at CSIS -- breaks down the global viability of the rare earths trade. Then, Quince Street Strategy Principal Tripp Hornick talks about the domestic-side of the investment, and what it means for companies trying take advantage in a growing industry. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nvidia’s Show of Financial Force Soothes Jittery Credit Markets
items.author: Caleb Mutua and Layan Odeh
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp.’s commitments to backstop the artificial intelligence boom seemed to be swelling by the day. There was the reported $250 billion to help kickstart a massive data center for OpenAI in Ohio, the latest in a string of big financings it was involved with.</article>

items.title: Phoebe Gates Knew Phia App Took Credit For Sales It Didn’t Drive
items.content: <article>Phia co-founders Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni pushed for features in the startup’s software that took credit for sales it didn’t drive. The founders were aware of the practice for at least seven months. Olivia Solon reports. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Former Hedge Fund CFO Pleads Guilty to Embezzling $3 Million
items.author: Bob Van Voris
items.content: <article>The former chief financial officer of a Miami Beach hedge fund admitted he embezzled more than $3 million over four years at the firm, approving phony invoices and using corporate credit cards for adult entertainment and personal travel.</article>

items.title: Trend-Chasing Funds’ Big Bond Short Raises Stakes for CPI
items.author: Ye Xie
items.content: <article>Record short bets against global bonds by trend-chasing investors are lifting the stakes for US inflation reports this week.</article>

items.title: NYSE Parent ICE Raises $3.75 Billion for MarketAxess Takeover
items.author: Brian Smith and Kevin Kingsbury
items.content: <article>Intercontinental Exchange Inc. sold $3.75 billion of US investment-grade bonds on Tuesday, less than two weeks after announcing a $6 billion deal to acquire MarketAxess Holdings Inc.</article>

items.title: Severe Storms Hit Chicago, Disrupt Hundreds of US Flights
items.author: Brian K. Sullivan and Emma Haidar
items.content: <article>Severe thunderstorms raked Chicago and the Midwest Tuesday, triggering tornado warnings and disrupting hundreds of flights as another round of dangerous weather swept across the US.</article>

items.title: Veritas-Owned Gainwell Begins Bond Part of $5.8 Billion Deal
items.author: Gowri Gurumurthy and Aaron Weinman
items.content: <article>Gainwell Technologies has started the next leg of a broader $5.8 billion debt overhaul that marks the US software sector’s biggest financing of 2026 in the junk-debt market.</article>

items.title: US Stocks End Down as Hormuz Deadlock Sends Oil Up Ahead of CPI
items.author: Norah Rami and Elena Eisenstadt
items.content: <article>US stocks continued to fall into Tuesday’s market close after Pakistan said a US and Iran deal to address the Strait of Hormuz was close, while negotiations between the two countries remain at an impasse, pushing oil prices higher.</article>

items.title: Yen Inches Toward 160 Per Dollar, Raising Intervention Concerns
items.author: Naomi Tajitsu and Anya Andrianova
items.content: <article>The yen edged closer toward a key level against the dollar, raising concerns over Japanese authorities stepping in again to prop up the currency.</article>

items.title: EM Assets Retreat as Iran Deal Doubts Push Oil Prices Higher
items.author: David Feliba, Beatriz Amat and Andras Gergely
items.content: <article>Emerging-market assets fell on Tuesday, with a currency gauge snapping a four-day winning streak as fading hopes for a US-Iran deal weighed on risk sentiment.</article>

items.title: Gold Slips From Two-Month High as Focus Shifts to Inflation
items.author: Preeti Soni and Yvonne Yue Li
items.content: <article>Gold declined from a two-month high as traders weighed prospects of a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while awaiting a key US inflation report that could provide fresh clues on the Federal Reserve’s appetite for an interest-rate hike.</article>

items.title: S&P 500 Falls as Oil Climbs Before Inflation Data: Markets Wrap
items.author: Rita Nazareth
items.content: <article>Wall Street traders refrained from making riskier bets before key inflation data, with stocks falling as the lack of a deal to restore energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz lifted oil prices.</article>
